argument.def: An input passed to a function, e.g. the 11 in print('fit', 11). Keyword arguments are passed by name (size=50), positional ones by order.

method.def: A function attached to an object and called with a dot, e.g. x.sum(); the object is passed in automatically.

attribute.def: A value attached to an object, read with a dot and no brackets, e.g. x.shape, x.dtype.

tuple.def: An ordered sequence in round brackets, like (2, 3), whose items cannot be changed.

random-seed.def: A number given to a random generator (np.random.default_rng(1303)) so the same 'random' numbers are produced every run.

slice.def: [start:stop:step]: items from start up to but not including stop, every step-th one.

boolean-index.def: Selecting entries with an array of True/False values of the same length: True entries are kept.

data-frame.def: A pandas table: columns of equal length, possibly of different types, with row and column labels.

na-values.def: Entries with no data, stored as np.nan; read_csv(..., na_values=['?']) converts a marker such as '?' into NaN.

lambda.def: A one-line unnamed function, e.g. lambda df: df['year'] > 80.

boxplot.def: A plot of the median, quartiles, whiskers and outliers of a variable, often side by side for each category of another variable.

scatter-matrix.def: A grid of scatterplots of every pair of variables, with each variable's histogram on the diagonal.
